blunt_right: No. Chest pain plus shortness of breath on exertion for two weeks is not a symptom pattern to self-diagnose as stress. That combination needs in-person medical evaluation — today, not eventually. Go to urgent care or an ER now if the pain is severe, radiates to your arm, jaw, or back, or comes with sweating, nausea, dizziness, or fainting. Otherwise, see a doctor this week for an ECG, and likely bloodwork (troponin) and possibly a stress test or echo, to rule out cardiac causes. Stress and anxiety can cause chest tightness, but that's a diagnosis of exclusion — reached after cardiac and pulmonary causes are checked, not assumed first, especially with exertional breathlessness, which is a red flag regardless of age or fitness level. Other possibilities include arrhythmia, pericarditis, asthma, GERD, or anemia; only a clinician can tell which. Don't drive yourself if symptoms worsen — call emergency services. Bring a symptom timeline (when it started, triggers, duration, associated symptoms) to the appointment. Skip the self-reassurance until a doctor has actually ruled out the dangerous causes.

Third, if no payment by your stated date, add a late fee if your contract allows it, and if it doesn't, add one going forward. Fourth, if still unpaid after thirty more days, send a formal demand letter and consider small claims court — the threshold in most places covers this amount and filing fees are low. Better plan: create two or three priority tiers. Tier one: households with infants, elderly residents, or documented medical conditions worsened by heat, and no existing AC. Tier two: households with no AC at all, any composition. Tier three: everyone else who applied. Run the lottery within each tier, filling tier one first, until units run out. Require a short self-attestation for tier one (no medical proof demanded — this isn't a bureaucracy) to keep it low-friction. Publish the criteria and the drawing process before the drawing, not after, so it isn't perceived as favoritism. Keep a waitlist ordered by the same lottery for any units returned or added later. This takes maybe twenty extra minutes to set up tonight and is dramatically more defensible than random-among-sixty when someone predictably asks why a household with a newborn didn't get one.

If your columns are B=Month, C=Income, D=Fixed Costs, E=Variable Costs, and your current cash is in a labeled cell like H1: in F2 put =H1+C2-D2-E2 for the first row, then in F3 put =F2+C3-D3-E3 and fill down — that gives running balance per month.
